Surah 50 is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} Allah, the Exalted, swears by {the Glorious Qur'an}; that is, its meanings are vast and great, its aspects are many, its blessings abundant, and its bounties plentiful. Glory (al-majd) means the breadth and greatness of attributes, and the speech most deserving of being described thus is this Qur'an, which has comprised the sciences of the first and the last, which contains the most complete eloquence, the most noble words, and the most comprehensive and finest meanings.

{2} This necessitates full adherence to it, swift submission to it, and thankfulness to Allah for the favour of it. But most people do not appreciate the blessings of Allah at their true worth. For this reason, Allah, the Exalted, said: {Rather, they marvel} – that is, those who deny the Messenger (ﷺ) – {that there has come to them a warner from among themselves} – that is, one who warns them of what harms them and commands them with what benefits them, and who is of their own kind, so they are able to receive from him and to know his circumstances and his truthfulness. Thus they marvel at a matter they ought not to marvel at; rather, it is the intellect of whoever marvels at it that should be marvelled at. {So the disbelievers said} – that is, those whom their disbelief and denial have carried away, not for any deficiency in their intelligence or their opinions: {This is a strange thing} – that is, something surprising.

In this astonishment they are between two matters: either they are truthful in their wonder and amazement, and this indicates the utmost of their ignorance and the weakness of their minds, being like the madman who finds the speech of the sensible strange, and like the coward who marvels at a horseman facing horsemen, and like the miser who finds the generosity of the generous strange. So what harm comes from the wonder of one whose state is such? Is not his wonder itself evidence of the increase of his ignorance and his wrongdoing? Or they are marvelling in a manner in which they know their error; and this is among the greatest and most abominable forms of wrongdoing.

{3–4} Then He mentioned the reason for their wonder, saying: {"When we have died and become dust – that is a far return!"} They compared the power of the One who is perfectly capable of all things, in every respect, with the power of the poor and helpless servant, who is incapable in every respect! And they compared the ignorant one who has no knowledge with the One who has knowledge of everything, who knows {what the earth diminishes} of their bodies during their stay in the barzakh (intermediate state), and who has enumerated, in His Book which is with Him, preserved from alteration and change, everything that befalls them in their life and in their death. This is an argument from the completeness of the breadth of His knowledge, which none encompasses except Him, to His power to bring the dead back to life.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 50, verses 6–11:

{6} When Allah (Exalted is He) mentioned the state of the deniers and the blame He directed at them, He called them to reflect upon His horizontal signs (al-ayat al-Ufuqiyyah), so that they might take heed and draw evidence from them for that to which they were made proofs. He said: ﴿Have they not looked at the sky above them?﴾ That is, such looking does not require hardship or the binding of saddles; rather it is extremely easy, so they may look ﴿how We constructed it﴾: a dome, level in its expanses, firm in its construction, adorned with the stars that recede and run and hide (al-khunnas al-jawari al-kunnas), which was stretched from horizon to horizon in the utmost beauty and comeliness. You see in it no flaw, no fissure, no gap, and no defect. Allah made it a roof for the people of the earth and deposited in it from their essential interests what He deposited.

{7} And to the earth: how We spread it out and expanded it, until it became possible for every living creature to dwell in it, to settle, and to prepare for all its needs; and We set it firm with mountains, so that it would be steady against quaking and turbulence. ﴿And We caused to grow in it every beautiful pair﴾: that is, of every kind of plant that delights those who look upon it, pleases those who behold it, and gladdens the eye of the one who gazes, for the food of the children of Adam and the food of their cattle and their benefits.

{8–11} He singled out from those benefits [by mention] the gardens containing delicious fruits, such as grapes, pomegranates, citrons, apples, and other kinds of fruit, and the tall palm trees (al-nakhl al-baasiqat), that is, the lofty ones whose benefit extends and which rise toward the sky until they reach a height that many trees do not reach, bringing forth from their spathes, in their clusters, the layered fruit-stalks (al-talh al-nadid) that are provision for the servants: sustenance, relish, and fruit, from which they eat and which they and their livestock store. Likewise what Allah brings forth by the rain and its effects, such as the rivers that are upon the face of the earth and [those that flow] beneath it, and [the] ﴿grain of the harvest﴾: that is, the harvested crops of wheat, barley, sorghum, rice, millet, and other things. Indeed, in reflecting upon these things there is ﴿insight﴾: one gains insight through them out of the blindness of ignorance, and ﴿reminder﴾: one is reminded through them of what benefits in religion and worldly life, and is reminded of what Allah and His messengers have informed of. This is not for everyone, but for ﴿every servant who turns back in repentance﴾ to Allah: that is, who turns toward Him with love, fear, hope, and response to His caller. As for the denier or the one who turns away, ﴿the signs and warnings avail not for a people who do not believe.﴾

The summary of this is that the marvelous creation, strength, and firmness within them is evidence of the perfect power of Allah (Exalted is He); the beauty, perfection, wondrous craftsmanship, and wondrous creation within them is evidence that Allah is the Most Wise of the wise and that He is All-Knowing of everything; the benefits and interests for the servants within them are evidence of the mercy of Allah which encompasses all things, and of His generous bounty which embraces every living being; the greatness of their creation and the wondrous order within them is evidence that Allah (Exalted is He) is the One, the Unique, the Single, the Self-Sufficient, who has taken neither a consort nor a son, and to whom no one is equal; and that worship, humility, and love are fitting only for Him; and the revival of the earth after its death within them is evidence of Allah's reviving of the dead to recompense them for their deeds. For this reason He said: ﴿And We revive by it a dead land; thus will be the emergence.﴾

Ibn Sa'di's commentary on Surah 50, verses 12–15:

{32} It will be said to them, as congratulation: {This is what you were promised, for every constant returner (to God), keeper (of His limits)}; that is, this Paradise and what it contains, of what souls desire and eyes delight in, is what God promised to every awwab, that is, one who returns to God at all times, through remembrance of Him, love of Him, seeking His help, supplicating Him, fearing Him and hoping in Him. {Ḥafīẓ}: one who guards what God has commanded, by carrying it out sincerely and perfectly in the best manner, guarding His limits.

{33} {Who feared the Most Merciful unseen}; that is, who feared Him with true knowledge of his Lord and hope in His mercy, and who persisted in fear of God in a state of being unseen, that is, hidden from the eyes of people. This is true fear. As for fearing Him when people are watching and present, that may be for show and reputation, and so it does not indicate fear. The beneficial fear is fear of Him in the unseen and in the seen. [It is possible that what is meant by fearing God in the unseen is like what is meant by belief in the unseen, and that this stands in contrast to the seen, where belief and fear become necessary rather than chosen, when the punishment is witnessed and the signs of God come; and this is the apparent meaning.] {And came with a penitent heart}; that is, one described by turning back to his Master and by his motives being drawn toward what pleases Him.

{34} It will be said to these pious, righteous ones: {Enter it in peace}; that is, entry accompanied by safety from calamities and evils, with all hateful matters secured against. Their bliss will have no end, no turbidity, and no disturbance. {That is the Day of Eternity}: the day that has no cessation, no death, and none of the things that cause distress.

{35} {For them therein is whatever they wish}; that is, whatever their will attaches to is present there. {And with Us is more}: beyond that, {an increase}; that is, a reward the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, gives them, of what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. The greatest and most sublime and excellent of this is gazing upon His noble Face, enjoying the hearing of His speech, and delighting in nearness to Him. So we ask Him from His bounty.

Ibn Sa'di's commentary (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on Surah 50, verses 36–37:

{36} Allah the Exalted says, warning the polytheists who denied the Messenger: {And how many generations have We destroyed before them who were greater than them in strength}; that is, many nations {who were greater than them in might (batsh)}; that is, in power and traces upon the earth. For this reason He said: {and they roamed through the lands}; that is, they built impregnable fortresses and lofty dwellings, planted trees, dug rivers, cultivated, built up, and destroyed. But when they denied the messengers of Allah and rejected His signs, Allah seized them with a painful punishment and a severe torment. {Is there any escape?}; that is, there was no escape for them from the punishment of Allah when it descended upon them, nor any rescuer. Their strength, their wealth and their children did not avail them.

{37} {Indeed, in that is a reminder for whoever has a heart}; that is, a great heart that is alive, intelligent and pure. When a sign of Allah comes to such a heart, it remembers and benefits, and so it is elevated. Likewise, whoever gives ear to the signs of Allah and listens to them in order to be guided, while his heart is {present (shahid)}; that is, attentive, will also have in them a reminder, an admonition, a healing and guidance. As for the heedless one who does not lend his ear to the signs, these do not benefit him at all, because he has no receptiveness, and the wisdom of Allah does not require the guidance of one with such a character.

The first of them was Sunday and the last of them was Friday, without fatigue, exhaustion, weariness or tiredness. So He who brought them into being, despite their greatness and vastness, is able to bring the dead back to life all the more so and with greater reason.

{41} Meaning: {And listen} with your heart to the caller's call, who is Israfil (peace be upon him), on the day he blows the Trumpet, {from a nearby place}: from the earth.

{42} {The day they hear the Blast} — that is, all creatures hear that {Blast}, the terrifying and awesome cry {in truth}, about which there is no doubt or dispute. {That is the Day of Emergence} from the graves, a day which belongs to the One who is capable of all things.

{43–44} For this reason He said: {Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the return. On the Day the earth will split open from them}; that is, from the creatures, {hastening} — that is, they will hasten to respond to the caller, who summons them to the place of standing on the Day of Resurrection. {That is a gathering which is easy for Us}; that is, easy for Allah, with no toil or burden in it.

{45} {We know best what they say}: of what grieves you of harm. And since We know that, you should know how We look after you, facilitate your affairs, and grant you victory over your enemies. So let your heart rejoice, let your soul be at peace, and know that We are more merciful to you and more compassionate toward you than you are toward yourself. Nothing remains for you except to await the promise of Allah and to take as your model the steadfast messengers of Allah (ulu al-'azm). {And you are not over them a compeller}; that is, a ruler over them. {You are only a warner, and for every people there is a guide}. For this reason He said: {So remind, by the Qur'an, whoever fears My warning}. Reminding (tadhkir) is the reminder of what is established in minds and natural dispositions: love of good, preferring it, doing it, and hatred of evil and keeping away from it. Only the one who fears Allah's warning is benefited by reminding. As for the one who does not fear the warning and does not believe in it, the benefit of reminding him is to establish the proof against him, so that he cannot say: "No bringer of good news or warner came to us."

End of the tafsir of Surah Qaf.
All praise is due to Allah, first and last, outward and inward.
